question: The compound interest earned in 1 year on ₹4,80,000 at the rate of 20% per annum, compounded quarterly, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Quarterly Rate** = 20% ÷ 4 = **5%** (fractional value = 1/20)

For 1 year (4 quarters), the **Ratio** of Principal to Amount = 20⁴ : 21⁴

⇒ 1,60,000 : 1,94,481 | Interest units = 1,94,481 − 1,60,000 = **34,481**

⇒ Given 1,60,000 units = ₹4,80,000 → 1 unit = ₹3

⇒ **Compound Interest** = 34,481 × 3 = **₹1,03,443**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,03,443.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹4,80,000 | Rate (R) = 20% p.a. | Time (T) = 1 Year

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9705b123a43df3a70be9614cb285ca6df88cbeae9e718abe1e9ba2bd929ff6d.png] 

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 20% ÷ 4 = 5%

⇒ Number of Quarters (n) = 1 × 4 = 4

⇒ Amount (A) = 4,80,000 × (1 + 5/100)⁴

⇒ A = 4,80,000 × (21/20)⁴

⇒ A = 4,80,000 × (194481/160000)

⇒ A = 3 × 1,94,481 = ₹5,83,443

⇒ **Compound Interest** = 5,83,443 − 4,80,000 = ₹1,03,443

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,03,443.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded **quarterly**, the annual rate is divided by 4 (R/4) and the time in years is multiplied by 4 (4T).

Effective Rate of Interest

For 4 periods of 5% each, the **effective rate** is roughly 21.55% (calculated as [(1.05)⁴ − 1] × 100).

Successive Percentage Shortcut

For two periods, effective rate = x + y + (xy/100). For 5% and 5%, it is 10.25%. For four periods, apply this twice to 10.25%.
